class.name: rclgd
class.brief_description: Main entry point for the ROS 2 GDExtension.
class.description: The [rclgd] singleton is the core of the ROS 2 bridge for Godot. It manages the global ROS 2 context, the executor thread, and the lifecycle of ROS 2 nodes. Before using any other ROS 2 components, you must call [method init] to initialize the environment. [b]Executor modes:[/b] By default the ROS 2 executor spins in a separate thread (subscription, timer and action callbacks are deferred to the Godot main thread, so regular GDScript stays safe). Launch with [code]--ros-args -p use_separate_thread:=false[/code] to spin synchronously on the physics tick instead. [b]Simulation time:[/b] Launch with [code]--ros-args -p publish_sim_time:=true[/code] to make Godot the time source: the physics tick drives and publishes [code]/clock[/code], scaled by [code]Engine.time_scale[/code]. The standard [code]use_sim_time:=true[/code] instead makes node clocks (and timers) [i]follow[/i] [code]/clock[/code] — use it alone in a visualizer running next to an external simulator, or together with [code]publish_sim_time[/code] when the Godot app is itself the simulator. [b]Error handling:[/b] RCLGD errors break into the script debugger by default. Set the [code]rclgd/debug/break_on_error[/code] project setting to [code]false[/code] to only log them instead.

method.name: godot_to_ros_quat
method.description: Converts a rotation from the Godot axis convention to the ROS axis convention. This is the exact mapping used internally by [RosTfBroadcaster], so rotations you build by hand (e.g. for an [code]Odometry[/code] message) stay consistent with TF.

method.name: godot_to_ros_vector
method.description: Converts a vector from the Godot axis convention (-Z forward, +Y up) to the ROS axis convention (+X forward, +Z up). This is the exact mapping used internally by [RosTfBroadcaster].

method.name: init
method.description: Initializes the ROS 2 context and starts the executor. This method must be called once at the start of the application, usually in a main script's [code]_ready()[/code] function. Arguments provided in [param args] are passed to the ROS 2 initialization system (e.g., for remapping or parameter overrides).

method.name: ok
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the ROS 2 context is currently active and the executor is running.

method.name: ros_to_godot_quat
method.description: Converts a rotation from the ROS axis convention to the Godot axis convention. Inverse of [method godot_to_ros_quat] and the exact mapping used internally by [RosTfListener].

method.name: ros_to_godot_vector
method.description: Converts a vector from the ROS axis convention (+X forward, +Z up) to the Godot axis convention (-Z forward, +Y up). Inverse of [method godot_to_ros_vector] and the exact mapping used internally by [RosTfListener].

method.name: shutdown
method.description: Shuts down the ROS 2 context and stops the executor thread. This should be called when the application is closing to ensure a clean exit.

signal.name: ros_ready
signal.description: Emitted when the ROS 2 context has been successfully initialized and is ready to create nodes and communication interfaces.
